quote: Answers given before reasoning are noisier and occasionally reverse these rules.
When cues tie or conflict, default to Case 1, especially in the 'after reasoning' format.
When the cues are balanced or weak, it defaults to 'Case 1', which suggests a position bias, especially when the answer comes after reasoning.
When the evaluator is otherwise indifferent, it defaults to 'Case 1', especially when answering after reasoning.
